profile_md: Johns Hopkins has several distributed, school-level routes where student teams work for external sponsors, but no university-wide scheme was verified. The clearest is Mechanical Engineering Senior Design: a two-semester, 8-credit senior capstone in which teams build prototypes for industry, government and non-profit sponsors who fund and receive the work (2026 Design Day). Civil and Systems Engineering seniors work with community clients, and the BME Undergraduate Design Team (teams of 5-8 over about a year) takes challenges from clinicians and industry, though the external share is unclear. In business, Carey's Innovation Field Project (8-week MBA team consulting for corporate sponsors) and the Health Care Strategy Practicum are described on undated pages. SAIS practicums put teams of about four to work for outside clients (e.g. AECOM). MSEM projects and SOURCE's Connection Community Consultants (teams of 3-5, up to 8 weeks, for Baltimore community organisations; 2026-27 recruiting) add further routes. Most are programme-specific; only SOURCE is cross-school and extracurricular. Pava Center accelerators are venture-building, not client projects. Uncertain: current-year evidence for Carey and SAIS, compulsory status of capstones, and the science and Krieger arts and humanities areas, which were thinly searched. All sources are search-index extracts because jhu.edu pages returned 403 to WebFetch and curl.
gaps: Direct page text unavailable (403 from jhu.edu hosts via WebFetch and curl; not bypassed). Science and Krieger AHSS thinly searched; Nursing, Peabody, Medicine unsearched in depth; CLE consulting course, CityLab and further departmental capstones (ECE, CS, Chem/Biomolecular, Civil) likely exist; dated current-year evidence missing for Carey, SAIS, MSEM.
